glosses: A small thin branch of a tree or bush.

examples.text: They used twigs and leaves as a base to start the fire.

glosses: Somebody, or one of their body parts, not looking developed.

examples.text: You need to find a source of motivation and play off of that. Whether it be the jock in high school that always called you fat, or the guy who picked on you and called you a twig.

glosses: To realise something; to catch on; to recognize someone or something.

examples.text: He hasn't twigged that we're planning a surprise party for him.

I pray you now send me some dub, / A bottle or two to the needy. / I beg you won't bring it yourself, / The harman is at the Old-Bailey; / I'd rather you'd send it behalf, / For, if they twig you they'll nail you.

examples.text: Well, with fewer people doing two or three times the work, you may have already twigged to this.

At this point in our story, we first meet the fleet repair ship Kamchatka, who everyone would soon become regrettably familiar with. Eventually, someone twigged to the fact that absolutely nobody else could see so much as a seagull, let alone any exceptionally-lost Japanese torpedo boats. And, when nothing actually happened, Kamchatka refused to say that it was a false alarm, only that it had altered course and the torpedo boats had gone away.

glosses: To be realized and understood; to click.

examples.text: Dries had told us to bring at least twenty litres of water because there was no water in camp and very few tourists stayed there.
